issues.detail: The Vietnamese 'muốn lấy ai tùy ý' (wants to take anyone at will) changes the meaning of the Greek 'ω θελει γαμηθηναι' (whomever she wishes to be joined/married to). The Greek implies a choice of a person, whereas the Vietnamese phrasing suggests a lack of restriction on the act itself or a general 'anyone'. More importantly, the Vietnamese 'lấy ai' is slightly broader than the specific grammatical structure of 'whom [she] wishes to be married to'.

The Greek 'ελευθερα εστιν' (she is free) is rendered as 'thì vợ được tự do' (then the wife is free). While acceptable, the Vietnamese adds a slight emphasis on the result of the condition that is slightly more interpretive than the direct Greek statement.
